questions.enonce_markdown:
Justify the resurrection of Jesus in line with the Fourth Gospel.

(25 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Introduction.** To justify the resurrection in line with the Fourth Gospel is to show why John presents it as true and necessary. Christians believe that God raised Jesus; John gives witnesses, signs and Jesus' own words.

**1. The testimony of the empty tomb (20:1-10).** Mary Magdalene finds the stone removed. Peter and the other disciple run to the tomb and see the linen wrappings and the cloth that had been on his head, rolled up in a separate place. The beloved disciple "saw and believed". This suggests that the body was not stolen, since thieves would hardly unwrap it.

**2. Appearance to Mary Magdalene (20:11-18).** She meets Jesus, thinks he is the gardener, then recognises him when he calls her name. He tells her to say to the disciples that he is ascending to his Father and their Father.

**3. Appearance to the disciples (20:19-23).** On the evening of the first day, behind locked doors, he greets them with "Peace be with you", shows them his hands and side, breathes on them and says "Receive the Holy Spirit". The fear of the disciples becomes joy and mission: "As the Father has sent me, so I send you."

**4. The appearance to Thomas (20:24-29).** Thomas wants to touch the wounds; Jesus invites him to do so; Thomas confesses "My Lord and my God". Jesus blesses those who have not seen and yet believe. The story answers doubt and shows the reality of the risen body.

**5. The appearance in Galilee (21).** At the Sea of Tiberias Jesus eats with the disciples and restores Peter, which shows his continuing care for the community.

**6. The resurrection fits Jesus' claims.** In John Jesus says, "I am the resurrection and the life" (11:25) and raises Lazarus as a sign. He speaks of the destroyed temple raised in three days (2:19-22), says that he lays down his life to take it up again (10:17-18), and promises to see the disciples again (16:16-22). Without the resurrection these words would be empty.

**7. The effects.** The disciples are transformed from fear to bold witness, and John states that the signs are written "so that you may come to believe" (20:31).

**Conclusion.** John justifies the resurrection by eyewitness testimony, the physical evidence, the fulfilment of Jesus' words and the change in the disciples. It confirms who Jesus is and gives believers life.
